notes: Bendall reads the date as N.S. 381, with the middle figure doubtful (A.D. 1261). The colophon does not name the era, but N.S. is implied. Bendall's conversion is kept for ce_approx. The king's name is damaged: 'श्री [?] ह मालदेव'. One possible reading is Jayasīhamalladeva, who reigned about N.S. 391–394 (1271–1274 CE). If so, the doubtful middle figure could be 9, giving N.S. 391 (1271 CE). In 1261 the reigning king was Jayabhīmadeva, and his name does not fit '…ha malladeva'. This is unresolved. 'कारित' is taken to mean that the king commissioned the copy, but it could be only a formula of royal patronage. अञ्जार is probably aṅgāra (Tuesday). The scribe's name and his vihāra ('शके वैहारश्रीभिचु', perhaps Śākya-vihāra śrī-bhikṣu, or a corrupt 'śākyabhikṣu') are corrupt. The name could also be read Devamaṇi or Devamati.
